description: Strategic deconfliction of two operational intents (pair cases) and the authorisation decision of one intent against the CIS, the registry and the intents already authorised (decision cases). Pair: each intent is a priority, the instant its volumes were filed, the geoid undulation at its volumes and F3548 Volume4D volumes with W84 altitudes; the judgement converts the bands to AMSL (D-01) and decides conflict and precedence. The harness checks every pair both ways (A against B and B against A) and requires the same pair decision. Decision: the fixture request with the case's overrides, decided against the case's CIS features, registry answers, terrain, DSS and existing intents.
source: utm TASKS.md U-05 done-when (either order, same result; refusal names the item)

units.altitude: metres above the WGS84 ellipsoid (W84) as F3548 gives them
units.undulation_m: geoid undulation N, AMSL = HAE - N

tolerance.horizontal: 1 cm plus 1e-4 of the separation, towards conflict

contingency.procedure: land at the nearest landing site

cases.name: same-volume-first-come-a
cases.why: Two identical volumes at equal priority: the one filed first keeps the space (Art. 10(9)).

cases.name: same-volume-first-come-b
cases.why: The same pair filed the other way round: the first filed wins again, so filing A then B or B then A gives the same pair decision.

cases.name: same-instant-smaller-id-wins
cases.why: Filed at the same instant: the smaller id wins, so the pair decision never depends on the order of the check.

cases.name: special-operation-wins-filed-later
cases.why: A special operation (SERA Art. 4) has the higher priority and wins over a normal flight filed before it (Art. 10(8)).

cases.name: special-operation-wins-filed-earlier
cases.why: Priority decides before time: the special operation wins whichever was filed first.

cases.name: equal-special-priority-first-come
cases.why: Two special operations: equal priority falls back to first come, first served.

cases.name: disjoint-in-space
cases.why: Two squares about 2.2 km apart do not conflict.

cases.name: disjoint-in-time
cases.why: The same airspace one second after the first window ends: no common instant.

cases.name: touching-in-time
cases.why: Windows are closed intervals: one ending at 10:30 and one starting at 10:30 share that instant and conflict.

cases.name: disjoint-in-altitude
cases.why: Bands 0.5 m apart do not conflict without a vertical buffer.

cases.name: touching-bands
cases.why: A band ending at 150 m and one starting at 150 m touch and conflict (closed bands).

cases.name: vertical-buffer-on
cases.why: Bands 5 m apart conflict under a 10 m vertical buffer.

cases.name: vertical-buffer-off
cases.why: The same bands do not conflict without the buffer.

cases.name: altitude-in-amsl-not-hae
cases.why: Separation is judged in AMSL (D-01): 100-150 m HAE with N 20 is 80-130 m AMSL and 155-200 m HAE with N 30 is 125-170 m AMSL, which overlap although the HAE bands do not.

cases.name: polygons-share-an-edge
cases.why: Squares sharing an edge touch: outlines are closed sets.

cases.name: gap-50m-no-buffer
cases.why: About 50 m of clear air between the outlines and no buffer: no conflict.

cases.name: gap-50m-buffer-100m
cases.why: The same pair under a 100 m horizontal buffer conflicts.

cases.name: gap-50m-buffer-40m
cases.why: A 40 m buffer is less than the gap: no conflict.

cases.name: polygon-inside-polygon
cases.why: A small square wholly inside a larger one: no edges cross, containment decides.

cases.name: crossing-bars-no-vertex-inside
cases.why: Two thin bars crossing like a plus sign: no vertex of either is inside the other; the crossing edges decide.

cases.name: concave-notch-clear
cases.why: A square in the notch of a U-shaped polygon, clear of every edge, does not conflict although it is inside the bounding box of the U.

cases.name: circle-inside-polygon
cases.why: A circle whose centre is inside the polygon conflicts.

cases.name: circle-near-polygon-clear
cases.why: A circle whose centre is about 250 m east of the polygon with a 150 m radius stays clear.

cases.name: circle-reaching-polygon
cases.why: The same centre with a 300 m radius reaches the polygon: polygon against circle by geodesic distance (Z-11).

cases.name: circles-overlap
cases.why: Two 300 m circles about 500 m apart overlap.

cases.name: circles-apart
cases.why: Two 200 m circles about 500 m apart are about 100 m clear.

cases.name: circles-apart-within-buffer
cases.why: The same circles under a 150 m buffer conflict.

cases.name: antimeridian-overlap
cases.why: A polygon straddling the antimeridian and one inside it conflict: longitudes are unwrapped, the antimeridian is no edge.

cases.name: antimeridian-apart
cases.why: Squares either side of the antimeridian about 2.2 km apart do not conflict (not 40 000 km apart, and not overlapping).

cases.name: antimeridian-apart-within-buffer
cases.why: The same squares under a 3 km buffer conflict across the antimeridian.

cases.name: antimeridian-circle-polygon
cases.why: A 150 m circle centred 0.0005 degrees east of the antimeridian reaches a polygon ending 0.0005 degrees west of it, about 111 m away across the antimeridian.

cases.name: second-volume-conflicts
cases.why: Only the second volume of the first intent meets the other: every pair of volumes is judged.

cases.name: negative-horizontal-buffer-refuses
cases.why: A negative buffer refuses the check (E-15) even for intents far apart: an invalid threshold never disarms it.

cases.name: negative-vertical-buffer-refuses
cases.why: A negative vertical buffer refuses the check rather than shrinking the bands.

cases.name: far-apart-prefilter
cases.why: Intents in different countries are cleared by the box prefilter.

cases.name: authorised-outside-uspace
cases.why: Every check passes outside U-space airspace: authorised with a number and the policy's deviation thresholds; local deconfliction suffices (02 F5).

cases.name: exempt-c0-a1
cases.why: Open A1 with a C0 aircraft is outside the regulation's scope (Art. 1(3)): accepted voluntarily, no authorisation number, no thresholds.

cases.name: exempt-privately-built-under-250g
cases.why: A privately built aircraft below 250 g in A1 is outside the scope too.

cases.name: privately-built-250g-is-authorised
cases.why: At 250 g a privately built aircraft is in scope: authorised like any other flight, with a number.

cases.name: exempt-still-refused-by-prohibited-zone
cases.why: An exempt flight needs no authorisation, but the USSP never accepts, voluntarily or not, a volume over a PROHIBITED zone (CLAUDE.md rule 4; a deviation from the brief, which skips the zone check for exempt flights).

cases.name: cis-stale-outside-uspace
cases.why: A stale CIS cache refuses even outside U-space airspace: whether the volume is outside it is read from the stale cache itself (stricter than 02 F3, which names U-space airspace).

cases.name: cis-stale-inside-uspace
cases.why: A stale CIS cache inside U-space airspace refuses with cis_stale (02 F3).

cases.name: cis-outdated-refuses

outdated: zones version 2 held, not used: no X-Publisher-Signature

cases.why: A newer CIS version held untrusted (or refused, or notified and not pulled) means the picture is known to be old: no authorisation rests on it.

cases.name: registry-unknown-inside-uspace
cases.why: The registry does not hold the operator and the volume is inside U-space airspace: held pending_validation (02 F8).

cases.name: registry-unknown-outside-uspace
cases.why: Outside U-space airspace an unknown registry answer also holds the intent (a deviation from the brief's accepted-with-condition: an unverified registration is never authorised).

cases.name: registry-unavailable-holds
cases.why: The authority cannot be asked and nothing is cached: unknown with registry_unavailable, held (02 F5 failure rule).

cases.name: operator-suspended-refuses-item-10
cases.why: A suspended operator is refused, naming Annex IV item 10.

cases.name: uas-revoked-refuses-item-1
cases.why: A revoked UAS registration is refused, naming Annex IV item 1.

cases.name: uspace-ceiling-exceeded
cases.why: The volume reaches 530 m AMSL over ground as low as 400 m: 130 m above the ground, over the airspace's 120 m ceiling, so it is refused naming the airspace.

cases.name: uspace-ceiling-respected
cases.why: A volume up to 480 m AMSL over ground of at least 400 m stays within the 120 m ceiling: authorised inside U-space airspace.

cases.name: uspace-ceiling-not-judged-without-terrain
cases.why: Without the ground the height against the ceiling cannot be judged: refused, never passed (Z-09).

cases.name: uspace-requirements-unreadable
cases.why: An airspace whose Art. 3(4) requirements cannot be read cannot have its constraints applied: refused.

cases.name: uspace-dss-unavailable-pending
cases.why: Inside U-space airspace the intent is deconflicted through the DSS; while the DSS cannot be written it waits as pending_dss (02 F5).

cases.name: uspace-dss-unavailable-outside-proceeds
cases.why: Outside U-space airspace local checks suffice when the DSS is down (02 F5).

cases.name: prohibited-zone-overlap
cases.why: A PROHIBITED zone overlapping the volume in space, altitude and time refuses it, naming the zone (Art. 10(7)).

cases.name: prohibited-zone-below-the-volume
cases.why: A PROHIBITED zone up to 300 m AMSL under a volume from 480 m AMSL does not overlap it.

cases.name: prohibited-zone-wgs84-limit
cases.why: A WGS84 limit is compared with the volume's W84 band as given: a zone up to 499 m WGS84 is below a volume from 500 m W84.

cases.name: prohibited-zone-agl-not-judged
cases.why: A PROHIBITED zone up to 50 m AGL with no ground known counts as overlapping (Z-09): refused.

cases.name: prohibited-zone-agl-judged-clear
cases.why: The same zone over ground of at most 450 m tops out at 500 m AMSL, below a volume from 580 m AMSL.

cases.name: prohibited-zone-far-away
cases.why: A PROHIBITED zone 10 km away does not overlap.

cases.name: req-authorisation-without-ref
cases.why: A zone requiring an authorisation and no authorisation_ref: held pending_authority, nothing sent (spec Q12).

cases.name: req-authorisation-with-ref
cases.why: With an authorisation_ref the zone becomes a condition of the authorisation.

cases.name: conditional-zone-condition

features.message: Coordinate with the aerodrome before take-off

cases.why: A CONDITIONAL zone is a condition carrying the zone's message.

cases.name: restriction-active-refuses
cases.why: An active ANSP restriction overlapping the volume refuses it (Art. 10(7)).

cases.name: restriction-ended-ignored
cases.why: A restriction the ANSP ended no longer refuses.

cases.name: restriction-later-window
cases.why: A restriction that starts after the volume ends does not overlap in time.

cases.name: existing-intent-filed-first-wins
cases.why: An authorised intent filed earlier at equal priority holds the space: the new one is refused naming it (Art. 10(9)).

cases.name: special-operation-over-existing
cases.why: A special operation has precedence over an authorised normal flight: it is authorised and the other is flagged for an update (Art. 10(8), (10)).

cases.name: existing-special-operation-wins
cases.why: An authorised special operation keeps the space against a normal flight.

cases.name: existing-intent-clear-above
cases.why: An authorised intent 100 m above the volume does not conflict.

cases.name: invalid-buffer-refuses
cases.why: A negative deconfliction buffer refuses the check and so the intent, even with no other intent near (E-15).

cases.name: zero-deviation-threshold-refuses
cases.why: A zero deviation threshold cannot be given to an authorisation: refused, never disarmed (E-15).
